html:
Daniel Ortega is a Nicaraguan politician, leader of the Sandinista National Liberation Front. He led the revolutionary government in the 1980s and has been president again since 2007.

A guerrilla jailed under the Somozas, he became coordinator of the junta after the revolution and was elected president in 1984. He governed through the Contra war and lost the election of 1990 to Violeta Chamorro.

He returned to power in 2007 after a deal with his rivals, and with his wife Rosario Murillo, made co-president in 2025, took control of the courts, army and elections. Protests in 2018 were crushed, with over 300 killed. Opponents, priests and even old revolutionary comrades were jailed or stripped of citizenship and expelled. The former rebel against Somoza is now often compared to him, and hundreds of thousands have left Nicaragua.
